items.summary: Google Workspace now documents service-level access controls and action review rules for external agents connected through its MCP tools or command line.
items.why_now: The November 24 release moves Workspace MCP and its command line into general availability, with documented administrator controls and agent audit attributes.
items.practical_value: Pilot one external agent in a test group and confirm that a restricted action triggers review and leaves the expected audit record.
items.limitations: Google describes platform behavior, not independently measured protection or adoption. The external-agent review rules do not apply to standard app connections.
items.next_action: Seek independent administrator tests that distinguish policy settings, actual prompts, audit coverage and failures across approved and blocked actions.

evidence.title: Simplifying agent access while keeping organizations in control
evidence.review_depth: Google's dated release announcement confirms general availability of Workspace MCP servers and the official CLI alongside expanded controls. It supplies no independent operational outcomes.

evidence.title: Control which apps access Google Workspace data
evidence.review_depth: Administration documentation lists client-level service controls, four user-review categories for external agents, and audit fields for agent identity and approval. The page was updated November 24 UTC; original publication date is unverified.

novelty.reason: General availability brings service-level controls and action-specific human review to common workplace tools on a named access route.

evidence.reason: The release and administrator guide specify access modes, review categories and audit fields, but do not quantify control effectiveness.

independence.reason: Google now documents a separate implementation alongside earlier AWS and Microsoft approaches, but these are platform-authored accounts, not independent product audits.

momentum.reason: No repeated measurement of approval behavior or audit coverage uses the same denominator at two known dates.

relevance.reason: An administrator can test an external agent against one reviewable action and inspect the resulting access decision and log.

durability.reason: Separating identities, least-privilege access, action approval and audit evidence remains useful as models and connectors change.
